prior_findings.note: Crash/recovery semantics improved, but member-level before/during/after create/write/Sync crash cuts still need exact artifact, catalog, reopen, and zero-effect oracles.
Failure matrix still bundles multiple operations and does not map each errno/short/full-write-plus-uncertain-Sync to return class, poison scope, restart result, and side-effect assertions.
C1-C5 named IPC schedules, lock-holder crash, bounded waits, linearization and zero-side-effect assertions address the prior gap.
Native Linux/Windows runner metadata, filesystem scope, concrete assertions, evidence, and fail-on-skip requirements are specified.
E2E-PILOT-01..07 trace the later browser acceptance and state clearly that supervisor tests are insufficient.
Coverage profile/thresholds, platform adapter coverage, event schema, trace linkage and negative log scans are specified.

new_findings.title: Case ID width is inconsistent
new_findings.evidence: Section 2 requires a 256-bit random case ID; Section 7 requires an unallocated 16-byte ID represented as 32 hex characters.
new_findings.recommendation: Choose one ID width and align validators, lock names, golden vectors, collision tests, and capacity reasoning.

new_findings.title: SQLite OS file identity requirement conflicts with driver limitation
new_findings.evidence: Section 2.6 requires matching the OS file ID of the opened DB; Section 9 says the driver does not expose the actual SQLite-opened file identity and substitutes protected-directory/path checks.
new_findings.recommendation: Either define the trusted-account/protected-directory/path check as the actual invariant and test oracle, or provide a driver/VFS/hook that proves the SQLite connection uses the verified OS file identity.
